newsitem.title: USA: Parents of slain Colorado girl say they have leads.
newsitem.headline: Parents of slain Colorado girl say they have leads.

text.p: The parents of slain beauty pageant winner JonBenet Ramsey said on Tuesday they had received "a couple" of leads from callers to a telephone tip line they established.
On Sunday John and Patsy Ramsey took out advertisements in the local Boulder newspaper, outlining what they said was a possible profile of the killer of their 6-year-old daughter.

"We have received a couple of very important leads from the tip line which our investigators are pursuing," the Ramseys said in a statement on Tuesay, but they did not disclose any details about the leads.

Crime experts said the profile was a bit general, but the Ramseys said they plan to take out another ad and circulate more fliers this weekend that will feature what they called "critical" handwriting samples from a ransom note, particularly the letter "M."
The child's body was found Dec. 26 in the basement of the family's home in Boulder after her mother said she found a ransom note demanding $118,000.

No arrests have been made and no suspects named in the 7-month-long investigation. The parents have criticised the police for focusing their investigation on the family rather than seeking other leads.

"It is our hope that someone will recognise both the handwriting and the likely pre- and post-crime characteristics exhibited by the kliller and will call our tipline with their information," the Ramsey statement said.

According to the profile assembled by the Ramsey investigators, the killer may have increased his consumption of drugs or alcohol, may have turned to religion and probably quickly constructed an alibi following the crime.
